 Fear of failure gripping Tigers?
 Published : 23 October 2026
 • 
 Updated : 23 October 2026, 09:04
 • 
 CRICKET
 SHARE 
 Sports Reporter 
 Photo: ACB 
 Zimbabwe and Afghanistan today will contest the UAE ODI Tri-Series final while Bangladesh watch from the sidelines, left to rue a missed opportunity. After a 99-run thrashing by Zimbabwe, the Tigers still had a route to the final, but needed to beat Afghanistan first on Wednesday. 
 Instead, an early collapse and a failure to capitalise on chances to regain momentum left Bangladesh all out for 160 in a seven-wicket defeat that ended their campaign. The manner of the loss pointed to a team struggling to handle pressure, with fear of failure creeping into its game.
 Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source 
 “The team showed a fear of failure which significantly impacts how the game will be played. It was painful to see the approach in the Afghanistan game. It was becoming apparent during the game that fear of failure gripped them,” a team management official told The Daily Star.
 Bangladesh once dominated both Zimbabwe and Afghanistan, but that advantage has faded. They won 10 of 16 ODIs against Afghanistan through 2023 but have lost five in a row since November 2024, their worst run against them. The latest defeat leaves Afghanistan ahead 12-11 in 23 meetings. Zimbabwe have also won five of the last seven ODIs against Bangladesh, including two consecutive series.
 The concern extends beyond the tri-series. Bangladesh have won four of their last seven ODI series, against West Indies, Pakistan, New Zealand and Australia. All three defeats came away from home. Their last bilateral series win abroad was against Ireland in May 2023, and they have since lost six consecutive away series, including a 3-0 whitewash in the West Indies. They have won just four of their last 19 away ODIs.
 Stand-in skipper Tawhid Hridoy has also highlighted the gap between Bangladesh’s ambitions and their performances.
 “Whenever we play a big series, tri-nation, Asia Cup, or World Cup... personally, and as a team, everyone wants to win a trophy. This hunger is in everyone. We only say it, but our actions don't reflect it,” he said after the defeat that knocked Bangladesh out.
 Read more ‘We only say it, but our actions don't reflect it’ 
 The batting numbers underline the problem. Between 2010 and 2020, Bangladesh were bowled out inside 50 overs in 28 of 86 innings batting first, around 32 per cent. Since 2023, that figure has risen to 14 of 35 innings, or 40 per cent.
 Read more Musical chairs, same old batting blunders 
 ODI batting demands a balance between Powerplay aggression, consolidation through the middle overs and acceleration in the final 15. Yet Bangladesh’s top six against Afghanistan included four openers, leaving the batting order looking like square pegs in round holes.
 Nor has the team settled on alternatives. Seventeen batters have occupied positions four to seven in the past two years, with Saif Hassan, Jaker Ali, Afif Hossain, Nurul Hasan and Shamim Hossain appearing in and out of the side. Mosaddek Hossain, brought into the middle-order picture after a successful Australia series, has also struggled to retain his place after seven matches.
 Ahead of bigger ODI assignments, they need a settled middle order and the composure to recover when things go wrong. Otherwise, the fear of failure could continue to undermine their ambitions.
 Tigers’ worrying ODI trend 
 - Bangladesh won 10 of 16 ODIs through 2023 but have lost five consecutive matches since November 2024.
 - Bangladesh have lost five of their last seven ODIs against Zimbabwe, including defeats across the last two series.
 - Bangladesh have been bowled out inside 50 overs in 28 of 86 innings batting first between 2010 and 2020 (32%). Since 2023, that has risen to 14 of 35 innings (40%).
